subject: Request: limited remote forensics + residency carveout — exec approval needed
messages:
From: Sarah Holloway <sarah.holloway@blueharborhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: BlueHarbor Procurement <procurement@blueharborhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: BlueHarbor ask: limited remote forensics access + residency carveout

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. BlueHarbor is excited about Redwood, but our security and legal teams have two non-standard asks that we need signed-off before we can proceed to procurement:

1) Residency carveout: some PHI processing for research workloads must remain in our US-only VPC. We need a contractual statement that those workloads will be pinned to a US-only private deployment with egress restricted to our network ranges.

2) Limited remote forensics: in the event of an incident, BlueHarbor needs remote, read-only access to runtime logs and the ability for our forensics vendor to run a timeboxed remote session (brokered via our PAM). This is strictly for post-incident investigation; we need guardrails (no write access, defined window).

We understand these are concessions. We can accept standard indemnities and will not ask for source code escrow. Separately, procurement is asking whether Redwood can offer a start-up credit or discount tied to a 24-month commit — they’ve budgeted conservatively.

Attached is our security questionnaire and a short statement of the residency requirements.

Can you escalate for exec approval? We’re targeting an October 31 signature to align with our board approval.

Thanks,
Sarah Holloway
CISO, BlueHarbor Health

Attachments: BH_Security_Questionnaire.pdf, residency-note.pdf
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:12:00 -07:00

Sarah —

Appreciate the clear ask and the timelines. I’ll escalate this immediately to Deal Desk + Legal. A few quick commitments from our side while I loop people in:

- We can support US-only pinning for specified datasets/workloads via a Private deployment (VPC) and network ACLs.
- Remote forensics: we can enable timeboxed, read-only log access and optional screen-share sessions for verified vendors, but this will need an agreed PAM + audit trail.

We’ll come back with a proposed set of guardrails and any one-time operational fees. Note: non-standard residency / forensic access will likely need an executive exception and possibly a committed term for the pricing concession.

I’m copying Jordan (Deal Desk) to start pricing and Karthik/Law for technical/legal constraints. I’ll follow up within 24 hours with a proposal.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Team —

Forwarding BlueHarbor’s asks (below). TL;DR of the concession request and why we should consider:

- Residency carveout: US-only pinning for PHI research workloads; requires Private/VPC deployment and egress restrictions to their ranges.
- Remote forensics: timeboxed (max 90 days post-incident), read-only log export and brokered remote session for their vendor.
- Commercial: they’ve asked whether Redwood can provide either a start-up credit or a discount for a 24-month commit. They’re small but strategic in MedTech.

Operational impact / risk: enabling vendor remote sessions has operational and compliance implications. Legal will need to limit scope and require indemnities. Infrastructure/ops will need a playbook to provision the session and collect an auditable trail.

What I’m asking:
1) Legal: please draft minimal contract language for a VPC addendum and a forensics access appendix (see attached draft redline: Redline_BH_VPC_Addendum_v1.docx).
2) Deal Desk (Jordan/Karthik): recommended commercial concession (discount % and any one-time credit) and whether this can be approved at deal desk or needs VP sign-off.
3) Ops: a high-level list of runbook items and estimated one-time engineering effort.

Proposed quick answer for the customer while we escalate: offer US-only pinning + conditional, timeboxed remote forensics access subject to legal-approved appendix and a 24-month commit. Ask for a 3-5 business day turn for final docs.

I’ll bundle the request for Lauren’s sign-off after we have legal/commercial input.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 08:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BlueHarbor ask — commercial + ops notes

Hey team — quick take from Deal Desk / Tech Ops perspective:

Commercial recommendation:
- Term: 24 months commit as requested.
- Concession: approve an up-to-15% subscription discount (applied across committed capacity) + a one-time onboarding credit up to $15,000. Any deeper discount (>15%) needs VP approval.
- SLA: keep standard SLA; any further availability guarantees are out of scope.

Technical/ops notes:
- Forensics access can be implemented as: read-only log exports (S3-like export to customer-controlled bucket), and a brokered session using our support console with session recording. No shell or write access.
- Timebox: 90-day window post-incident for remote vendor access; after that, access only via formal legal request and audit.
- Effort estimate: small one-time engineering effort (~2 developer-weeks) and runbook + support training (~1 week). Recommend a one-time implementation fee.

Legal redlines are required around indemnity and data access scope — Kim, can you propose language?

I believe this is reasonable to approve at VP-level for discount above 15% or any carveouts that increase risk. If we keep concessions to 15% + $15k credit and the 90-day window, deal desk can sign.

—Karthik
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2026 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BlueHarbor ask — commercial + ops notes (EXEC DECISION)

Team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and clear options. I’ve reviewed the risk tradeoffs and will approve the concession with the following binding conditions:

1) Commercial: authorize a 12% subscription discount across the 24-month committed capacity plus a one-time onboarding credit of $12,500. Any increase to discount or additional credits require CFO sign-off.

2) Residency: Redwood will contractually bind the specified PHI workloads to a US-only Private deployment. Ops must document the network ranges and ACLs in the addendum.

3) Forensics access: approve timeboxed, read-only access for an approved vendor for up to 90 days post-incident. Access must be brokered by Redwood support through a recorded session; no direct write or admin privileges. The customer must provide proof of vendor identity and a signed vendor NDA.

4) Legal: required to add an explicit limitation-of-scope clause in the VPC addendum and require an indemnity for any misuse of remote sessions. Also add an audit clause allowing Redwood to revoke access immediately if suspicious activity is detected.

5) Fees: Ops to propose a one-time implementation fee to cover runbook and engineering effort; include this in the SOW.

Marissa — please inform the customer of the approved terms and attach the legal addendum once Kim has redlined it. Jordan/Karthik — proceed to prepare the quote reflecting the 12% discount and $12.5k credit. I’ll sign the exec approval memo so Legal can proceed with the addendum.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
